breakfast.name: Piadina (Flatbread)
instructions: Mix dough, rest
Roll thin circles
Cook on griddle until spotted
Fill with prosciutto, cheese, arugula
breakfast.description: Thin flatbread stuffed with cured meats and cheese.

breakfast.name: Cappuccino e Cornetto
instructions: Steam milk for cappuccino
Warm cornetto
An Italian-style breakfast
breakfast.description: Coffee and pastry — the standard San Marinese morning.

breakfast.name: Crescioni (Fried Flatbreads)
ingredients: Water, salt, lard or olive oil
Filling: spinach and cheese, OR radicchio, OR sausage
instructions: Crescioni are San Marinese fried flatbreads -- the street food of the republic
Small, round flatbreads filled with savory fillings and pan-fried
The spinach and stracchino (soft cheese) filling is the classic
Radicchio and squacquerone (another soft cheese): the second classic
The dough is wrapped around the filling and sealed
Fried on a flat pan (testo) until golden on both sides
The testo is the traditional Romagnola cooking vessel for crescioni
breakfast.description: San Marinese fried flatbreads -- small circles of dough filled with spinach and soft cheese (or radicchio) and pan-fried on a testo (the traditional flat pan) until golden. The street food of the Republic of San Marino. The filling is enclosed inside the dough, not on top.

breakfast.name: Coffee and Cornetto
ingredients: Espresso (made in a moka pot or espresso machine)
Cornetto (the Italian croissant -- softer and sweeter than French croissant)
instructions: San Marino is geographically inside Italy -- its food culture is deeply Italian
The morning espresso and cornetto is the Italian ritual, also the San Marinese ritual
Espresso at the bar (the Italian coffee bar): standing, quickly, before work
The cornetto: the Italian breakfast pastry -- softer, more brioche-like than French croissant
Filled with cream, jam, or nothing (vuoto = empty)
breakfast.description: San Marinese (Italian-style) breakfast -- espresso at the bar and a cornetto (the Italian croissant: softer and sweeter than French, filled with cream or jam). San Marino is surrounded by Italy and shares the Italian morning bar ritual: coffee standing, quickly, before work.

lunch.name: Pasta e Ceci (Pasta with Chickpeas)
instructions: Sauté garlic and rosemary in olive oil
Add chickpeas and tomato paste
Add water, bring to boil
Add pasta, cook until done
Serve with Parmesan

lunch.name: Nidi di Rondine (Swallow's Nests)
instructions: Make thin pasta sheets
Fill with ham, cheese, béchamel
Roll up, slice into nests
Top with meat sauce and cheese
Bake at 180°C 30 min
lunch.description: Rolled pasta 'nests' with ham, cheese, and meat sauce — San Marino's signature.

lunch.name: Strozzapreti al Ragu
ingredients: Strozzapreti pasta (hand-rolled, twisted pasta -- the regional shape)
Ragu: beef, onion, tomato, red wine
instructions: Strozzapreti means priest-stranglers -- a joking reference to the greedy clergy
The pasta is rolled and twisted by hand
The twist: the dough is rolled on the board with both hands pushing in opposite directions
The rough surface of the pasta catches the ragu
San Marino and Romagna (the surrounding Italian region) share this pasta
lunch.description: San Marinese priest-strangler pasta -- strozzapreti (hand-twisted pasta, the name means priest-strangler) with beef ragu. The hand-rolling gives a rough surface that catches the sauce. Shared with the surrounding Romagnola region.

lunch.name: Fagioli con le Cotiche (Beans with Pork Rind)
instructions: Fagioli con le cotiche is the cucina povera of San Marino and Romagna
Beans with pork rind -- the peasant dish that transforms nothing into richness
The pork rind slowly releases gelatin as it cooks
The beans absorb the gelatin and the smoky pork flavor
The broth thickens into a rich, silky bean stew
lunch.description: San Marinese beans with pork rind -- borlotti beans simmered with pork rind (cotiche) until the rind releases gelatin into the broth, thickening it. The beans absorb smoky pork richness. Cucina povera: the peasant tradition of transforming inexpensive ingredients.

lunch.name: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
instructions: Bruschetta is the simplest Italian food -- grilled bread with tomato
The bread is grilled or toasted
Rubbed with raw garlic while still hot -- the heat opens the garlic
Topped with ripe tomatoes, basil, and the best olive oil available
The quality of the olive oil determines the quality of the bruschetta
lunch.description: San Marinese bruschetta -- bread grilled, rubbed with raw garlic while hot, topped with ripe chopped tomatoes, fresh basil, and extra-virgin olive oil. The quality of the olive oil is everything in bruschetta.

dinner.name: Coniglio alla Sammarinese (Rabbit)
instructions: Brown rabbit pieces in olive oil
Add garlic, rosemary, fennel seeds
Deglaze with white wine
Braise 45 min until tender
dinner.description: San Marinese braised rabbit with fennel and white wine.

dinner.name: Torta Tre Monti (Wafer Cake)
instructions: Layer wafer sheets with chocolate-hazelnut cream
Coat in dark chocolate
Chill until set
Cut into small cakes
dinner.description: The famous three-tower wafer cake — named for San Marino's three peaks.

dinner.name: Nidi di Rondine (Swallow Nest Pasta)
instructions: Nidi di rondine (swallow nests) is the signature San Marinese pasta dish
Unique to San Marino -- not found in surrounding Italian regions
Thin egg pasta sheets are layered with prosciutto and cheese
Rolled into a cylinder
Sliced into rounds -- the cross-section resembles a bird's nest
Baked with bechamel sauce and parmesan
dinner.description: San Marino unique pasta dish -- thin egg pasta sheets layered with prosciutto and gruyere, rolled into a cylinder, sliced into rounds revealing a nest cross-section, baked in bechamel. Unique to San Marino; not found in surrounding Italy.

dinner.name: Coniglio in Porchetta (Rabbit Roasted Like Porchetta)
instructions: Coniglio in porchetta applies the porchetta technique to rabbit
Porchetta: the whole pig roasted on a spit with fennel, garlic, and herbs
The rabbit version: the rabbit is stuffed with fennel, garlic, and herbs like a porchetta
Larded with pancetta for moisture
Roasted until golden
Wild fennel is essential -- the ferula fennel of the hillsides
dinner.description: San Marinese rabbit roasted like porchetta -- rabbit stuffed with wild fennel, garlic, rosemary, and pancetta (the porchetta technique applied to rabbit), roasted until golden. Wild fennel from the hillsides is essential; it gives the dish its distinctly aromatic character.

dinner.name: Piadina Romagnola
ingredients: Flour, lard (or olive oil), water, salt, baking soda
Filling: squacquerone cheese and prosciutto, OR arugula and stracchino
instructions: Piadina is the Romagnola flatbread -- the most common food of the surrounding region
San Marino, surrounded by Romagna, shares the piadina tradition completely
Unleavened (or slightly leavened) flatbread cooked on the testo (flat pan)
Filled and folded in half -- the piadina is a wrap
The classic filling: squacquerone (a very soft, spreadable cheese) and prosciutto crudo
The arugula and stracchino combination: the alternative classic
Piadinerie (piadina shops) are everywhere in Romagna and San Marino
dinner.description: San Marinese Romagnola flatbread -- unleavened dough cooked on a testo (flat pan), filled with squacquerone (very soft spreadable cheese) and prosciutto crudo, then folded. Or with arugula and stracchino. San Marino is surrounded by Romagna and shares its piadina tradition completely.

snacks.name: Crescioni (Stuffed Flatbread)
instructions: Make piadina dough
Fill with greens or cheese
Fold in half, seal edges
Cook on griddle until golden

snacks.name: Cicoli Fritti (Fried Lard Crackling)
ingredients: Cicoli (rendered pork fat crackling from lard production)
instructions: Cicoli are the crispy fried pork crackling produced during lard rendering
When lard is rendered, the solid pork pieces become crispy as the fat liquefies
These crispy pieces (cicoli) are the by-product and the snack
Salty, crispy, intensely porky
Eaten warm as a snack or folded into piadina dough
snacks.description: San Marinese pork crackling -- the crispy solid pieces produced when rendering lard, salted and eaten warm. Intensely porky and crispy. Also folded into piadina dough as a filling.

snacks.name: Castagne Arrostite (Roasted Chestnuts)
instructions: Chestnut roasting in autumn: a universal Italian tradition, shared by San Marino
The chestnuts are scored on the flat side before roasting
Roasted in a perforated chestnut pan over fire or in the oven
The split reveals the cooked nut inside
San Marino chestnut forests exist on Mount Titan
snacks.description: San Marinese autumn roasted chestnuts -- scored and roasted over fire in a perforated pan until the skin splits and the sweet nut inside is cooked. Chestnut forests exist on Mount Titan. An autumn ritual shared with all of Italy.

snacks.name: Torta di Tre Monti (Three Hills Cake)
instructions: Torta di Tre Monti is San Marino signature sweet -- named after the Three Towers (Tre Colli)
A layered wafer cake filled with chocolate cream and coated in chocolate
The three towers of San Marino: Guaita, Cesta, and Montale -- the symbols of the republic
Sold in every San Marinese patisserie and gift shop
The gift from San Marino -- taken home by every tourist
snacks.description: San Marino signature wafer cake -- layers of wafer filled with chocolate cream and coated in chocolate, named after the Three Towers (Tre Colli) that symbolize the republic. Sold in every San Marinese patisserie; the souvenir taken home by every visitor.

desserts.name: Bustrengo (Fruit Cake)
instructions: Mix breadcrumbs and cornmeal
Add fruits, nuts, honey, eggs
Pour into pan, bake at 175°C 45 min
desserts.description: Ancient fruit and nut cake with honey.

desserts.name: Bustrengo
instructions: Bustrengo is the traditional San Marinese winter cake -- cucina povera
A dense cake that uses day-old bread as a primary ingredient
Sweetened with honey and dried fruit
Studded with walnuts and pine nuts
The lemon zest and cinnamon give it its fragrant character
Similar to the Romagnola bustrengo -- shared across the region
desserts.description: San Marinese winter bread cake -- day-old bread and cornmeal with dried figs, raisins, walnuts, honey, and lemon zest baked into a dense, fragrant cake. Cucina povera: the bread is the base, not the flour. Shared with the surrounding Romagnola region.

desserts.name: Zuppa Inglese
ingredients: Pan di Spagna (sponge cake) or ladyfingers
instructions: Zuppa inglese (English soup) -- confusingly named, it is an Italian dessert
The name is disputed: possibly inspired by English trifle, or named after the English tourists
Layers of sponge cake soaked in Alchermes (the red liqueur) with custard
The Alchermes is the essential element -- its bright red color and flavor
A traditional Italian dessert shared across Romagna and San Marino
desserts.description: San Marinese Italian trifle -- sponge cake soaked in Alchermes (the bright red Italian liqueur), layered with custard cream (crema pasticcera). The Alchermes is the essential element: without it, it is not zuppa inglese. Shared across Romagna and San Marino.

drinks.name: Moscato di San Marino
instructions: Serve chilled
Sweet, sparkling local wine
drinks.description: Sweet sparkling Moscato from San Marino's tiny vineyards.

drinks.name: Limoncello
instructions: Infuse lemon zest in vodka 2 weeks
Mix with sugar syrup
Chill, serve ice cold
drinks.description: Bright lemon liqueur — served as digestif.

drinks.name: Sangiovese di San Marino
instructions: San Marino produces its own wine from Sangiovese grapes
The same grape as Chianti, Brunello di Montalcino, and Morellino di Scansano
San Marinese Sangiovese: grown on the slopes of Mount Titan
Dry red wine with cherry fruit, earthy, and slight tannin
San Marino has its own DOC (Denominazione di Origine Controllata)
The wine is not exported much -- mostly consumed within the tiny republic
drinks.description: San Marinese Sangiovese wine -- grown on the slopes of Mount Titan, the same grape as Chianti. San Marino has its own DOC. Dry red with cherry fruit and earthiness. Mostly consumed within the republic; rarely exported.
